title: Adaptive Rerank Budgeting for Video-Text Retrieval via Layer-Disagreement Routing

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is "无须训练地量化检索查询不确定性" (training-free quantification of retrieval query uncertainty). This aligns with the general goal of query performance prediction (QPP), which estimates retrieval quality or query difficulty. Paper [6] ("Query performance prediction") and paper [17] ("Noisy Perturbations for Estimating Query Difficulty in Dense Retrievers") both address QPP, with [17] specifically targeting dense retrievers. Paper [8] ("QUARK: Robust Retrieval under Non-Faithful Queries via Query-Anchored Aggregation") also formalizes retrieval under recall noise, modeling query uncertainty. These papers share the same objective of quantifying query uncertainty, making the purpose covered.

### Mechanism
The contribution's mechanism is "跨层 ranking disagreement (层间 top-k 候选集 Jaccard 距离)" (cross-layer ranking disagreement using Jaccard distance between top-k candidate sets). Paper [7] ("CA-Jaccard: Camera-aware Jaccard Distance for Person Re-identification") uses Jaccard distance for re-ranking and clustering, and paper [19] ("Fuzzy Jaccard Index") proposes a robust Jaccard-based similarity measure for ranked lists. While these papers use Jaccard distance in different contexts, the underlying primitive — measuring overlap between ranked sets — is equivalent. Paper [15] ("Impact of assessor disagreement on ranking performance") also discusses ranking disagreement, though in the context of inter-assessor variability. These prior works cover the mechanism.

### Evaluation
The contribution's evaluation compares the proposed signal (cross-layer ranking disagreement) against margin-based signals. Paper [17] ("Noisy Perturbations for Estimating Query Difficulty in Dense Retrievers") evaluates query difficulty estimation methods for dense retrievers, which involves comparing signals for retrieval quality. Paper [6] ("Query performance prediction") and paper [30] ("Learning-based Query Performance Modeling and Prediction") also evaluate QPP methods, using similar designs to compare predictive signals. These prior papers share the evaluation design, making it covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of video-text retrieval. Papers [1] ("Multi-event Video-Text Retrieval"), [2] ("VideoCLIP"), [3] ("Robust Video-Text Retrieval Via Noisy Pair Calibration"), and [5] ("Debiased Video-Text Retrieval via Soft Positive Sample Calibration") all address video-text retrieval, making the domain covered.

**PURPOSE: Training-free quantification of retrieval query uncertainty**

Paper [17] proposes "an unsupervised QPP method for dense neural retrievers" — QPP (Query Performance Prediction) is essentially quantifying query uncertainty/difficulty in retrieval without supervision. Paper [6] and [13] also address query performance prediction. Paper [25] addresses "Query Performance Prediction" for neural retrievers. The purpose of estimating how uncertain/difficult a query is for a retrieval system, without training, is substantively equivalent to QPP — same objective at the problem-class level. Paper [8] (QUARK) also addresses "training-free framework for robust retrieval" by modeling query uncertainty. These papers cover the purpose of training-free query uncertainty quantification in retrieval.

**MECHANISM: Cross-layer ranking disagreement via Jaccard distance between top-k candidate sets across layers**

Paper [17] proposes QPP via "noisy perturbations" to estimate query difficulty — different mechanism (perturbation-based, not cross-layer). Paper [7] uses Jaccard distance for person re-ID re-ranking, but not cross-layer disagreement. Paper [19] proposes "Fuzzy Jaccard Index" for comparing ordered lists. Paper [26] "query by committee" uses disagreement among committee members as a signal — conceptually related but different primitive (committee of models vs. layers). None of the prior papers specifically use cross-layer ranking disagreement (Jaccard distance between top-k sets from different layers of the same model) as the mechanism. The closest is [17] which uses perturbation-based list instability, but the specific primitive of measuring inter-layer top-k Jaccard disagreement within a single model is not present. Paper [7] uses Jaccard distance in retrieval but for camera-aware re-ranking, not cross-layer uncertainty. No paper combines cross-layer comparison + Jaccard distance on top-k sets for uncertainty estimation.

**EVALUATION: Comparison against margin-based signals**

Paper [17] evaluates QPP methods and compares against baselines including margin/score-based signals — "we propose an unsupervised QPP method... which operates by redefining the well-known concept of query clarity." QPP papers [6], [13], [25] all compare against various baseline signals including margin/score-based ones. This evaluation design (comparing a proposed uncertainty/difficulty signal against margin-based baselines) is standard in QPP literature and appears in [17] and [25].

**DOMAIN: Video-text retrieval**

Papers [1], [2], [3], [5] all explicitly work in video-text retrieval. This domain is clearly covered.

### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is "adaptive allocation of rerank budget based on query difficulty." Paper [4] ("AcuRank: Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Computation for Listwise Reranking") explicitly addresses adaptive reranking based on query difficulty and document distribution, which is substantively equivalent to the contribution's purpose. Paper [8] ("A budget-adaptive allocation rule for optimal computing budget allocation") also discusses adaptive budget allocation, but in the context of simulation-based ranking and selection, which is not directly tied to reranking pipelines or query difficulty. Therefore, [4] is the closest match.

### Mechanism
The contribution's mechanism is "3-tier routing maps disagreement scores to K∈{10,60,100}." Paper [4] ("AcuRank") describes an adaptive reranking framework that dynamically adjusts computation based on query difficulty, which involves routing and adaptive allocation strategies. While the specific implementation (e.g., disagreement scores mapped to tiers) differs, the underlying primitive of adaptive routing based on query characteristics is substantively equivalent. No other paper describes a mechanism that matches this level of equivalence.

### Evaluation
The contribution uses "MSR-VTT/DiDeMo R@1" as its evaluation design. Paper [23] ("AutoArabic") explicitly mentions MSR-VTT and DiDeMo benchmarks for video-text retrieval, which matches the benchmark family. Additionally, R@1 is a standard retrieval metric used in video-text retrieval tasks, and prior papers like [28] ("MV-Adapter") and [33] ("A Novel Convolutional Architecture For Video-Text Retrieval") also use similar benchmarks and metrics. Therefore, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of video-text retrieval. Papers [23] ("AutoArabic"), [27] ("Cmu-ucr-bosch @ Trecvid 2017"), [28] ("MV-Adapter"), [33] ("A Novel Convolutional Architecture For Video-Text Retrieval"), and [35] ("Multi-event Video-Text Retrieval") all work in the same general application area of video-text retrieval. While the specific datasets or sub-problems may differ, the domain is clearly covered.
